key_insight: EHRAdapt maps structured EHR events directly into a frozen language model using a semantic prior plus a learned residual, which helps especially with rare clinical events.
clinical_relevance: This could improve prediction and downstream classification from EHRs without forcing records into long text strings, potentially making rare disease signals easier to detect.
method: Takes (time, modality, code) EHR tuples and embeds them into the LLM input space.
Uses learned modality embeddings and attention biases for time gaps.
Represents each event code as a frozen semantic prior from clinical ontology descriptions plus a low-rank evidence residual that updates with observed data.
evidence_signal: Continued pretraining on about 4 million patients' records with frozen OLMo2 1B, Llama3.2 1B, and OLMo2 7B backbones showed the full adapter outperforming ablations on next-event prediction and downstream infectious-disease/syndromic classification.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable clinical code descriptions and adapter training on large EHR corpora, so performance and portability may vary across health systems and coding schemes.
paper_title: EHRAdapt: Adapting Pretrained Language Models to Electronic Health Records with Semantic Priors for Rare Clinical Events
